Why ClearHelp is different
Every resource is vetted

Results show their source, service area, and last-check status. A broad or unconfirmed listing is labeled honestly instead of being presented as verified local help.

No fake coverage

If a city or category doesn't have enough verified data, we say so honestly rather than padding results with unconfirmed listings.

Real guidance, not just listings

Each category explains what help covers, what to bring, and what to expect — so you know what you're walking into.

Connected pathways

Need food AND help with rent? We connect related categories so you can find everything in one search, not a dozen separate websites.

How ClearHelp works

We connect useful resources. Government databases, nonprofit registries, 211 networks, and reviewed community listings.

Free to use. No ads. No sign-up required. No data selling. Ever.

Not for emergencies. Call 911 if you're in danger. For resource help, call 211.

WHERE LISTINGS COME FROM

Federal and state program databases, nonprofit registries, 211 networks, community health directories, and reviewed community submissions.

WHEN THEY WERE LAST CHECKED

Verified resources show a check date. Records marked unverified have not been independently confirmed — call ahead before visiting.

WHAT "VERIFIED" MEANS

A verified resource has had its contact information, hours, and services confirmed through a direct source — a government registry, official website, or direct outreach.

COVERAGE STATUS

ClearHelp accepts assigned ZIP codes across all states, D.C., and U.S. territories. Local depth is strongest in 13 metro markets; elsewhere, results may be state, territory, remote, or national when the source explicitly confirms that reach.Call 211 where available if local results are limited or you need more options right away.

HOW TO REPORT A CHANGE

If a phone number, address, or service has changed, use the
REPORT AN ISSUE
link on any resource card. We review all reports.
